mainTopic: Completing the weekly פרשה with the ציבור, fathers' advice to their sons, and the latest time for the night קריאת שמע
overview: The amud opens by finishing a teaching: you must complete the weekly פרשה with the ציבור, reading the מקרא twice and the תרגום once, even a verse of place names like "עטרות ודיבן". The reward is long life. רב ביבי בר אביי tries to make up a year's missed פרשיות on ערב יום כפור, but he is told that eating on that day is a מצוה worth as much as fasting. When he then tries to read ahead, an elder teaches that the reading must be neither early nor late. The גמרא then lists practical advice that רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבא gave their sons, including the rule against passing behind a בית הכנסת during davening, which אביי limits in three ways. Two ברייתות praise the good manners of the מדיים and the modesty of the פרסיים, followed by a harsh teaching about the פרסיים. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה: the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל that the night שמע lasts until dawn. It discusses two ברייתות of רבי שמעון בן יוחי about reading שמע twice, around dawn and around sunrise. The contradiction in the second ברייתא is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: Even a verse of place names must be read, and the reward is long life
steps.stepSummary: The rule of reading the פרשה twice plus תרגום once applies even to "עטרות ודיבן". Whoever completes his פרשיות with the ציבור is rewarded with long life.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even the verse "עטרות ודיבן" must be read this way. For anyone who completes his פרשיות together with the ציבור has his days and years lengthened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the statement quoted on the previous amud: you must complete your weekly פרשה with the ציבור. It adds that no verse is skipped, and it gives the reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "עטרות ודיבן" (במדבר ל״ב:ג) is a verse made only of place names. In תרגום those names come out almost exactly the same, so you might think there is no point in reading it again. The גמרא says you still read it, which shows the obligation covers the whole פרשה, every verse. The reward of long life explains why this matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Opening words of a verse (Numbers 32:3) that lists only place names
One who completes his weekly Torah portions
Together with the congregation, in step with their reading schedule
His days and years are lengthened (long life)

steps.confusionAlert: The word "ואפילו" ("and even") continues a statement that began on the previous amud: "one should always complete his פרשיות with the ציבור, twice מקרא and once תרגום." Without that background, this line looks like it starts from nowhere.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for the practice of שנים מקרא ואחד תרגום. It shows the practice covers every single verse of the פרשה.

phrases.english: And even the verse "Atarot and Divon"
phrases.notes: A verse of place names, which are the same in the Hebrew and in the Aramaic translation

phrases.english: for anyone who completes his portions with the congregation
they lengthen for him his days and his years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier statement (on the previous amud) about completing the פרשיות with the ציבור
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every verse must be read twice plus תרגום once, even a verse of names, and completing with the ציבור brings long life.

steps.title: רב ביבי plans to catch up on all the year's פרשיות on ערב יום כפור
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי intended to make up all the פרשיות he had missed during the year on ערב יום כפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי thought to complete the פרשיות of the entire year on ערב יום כפור.
steps.whatsHappening: A story begins. רב ביבי בר אביי proposes a plan to catch up on missed פרשיות all at once. This step sets up the objection that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His idea makes sense on the surface. If he missed some פרשיות during the year, ערב יום כפור seems like a good, holy time to finish them before the new judgment. The question underneath is whether a late make-up counts, and whether this particular day is the right time for it.

keyTerms.meaning: ערב יום כפור, the day before יום כפור

phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye thought
to complete the portions of the whole year
on the eve of Yom Kippur,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי סָבַר לְאַשְׁלוֹמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule of completing the פרשיות to a practical case of making them up late
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposed practice: make up a year of missed פרשיות on ערב יום כפור.

steps.title: חייא בר רב מדפתי objects with a verse about the ninth of תשרי
steps.stepSummary: חייא בר רב מדפתי quotes the verse "ועניתם את נפשתיכם בתשעה לחדש בערב" against רב ביבי's plan.
steps.simpleTranslation: חייא בר רב מדפתי taught him: It is written, "And you shall afflict your souls on the ninth of the month in the evening."
steps.whatsHappening: Someone pushes back on רב ביבי's plan by quoting a פסוק about יום כפור. The point of the verse is not yet clear, so this step sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse (ויקרא כ״ג:ל״ב) mentions "the ninth" day, which is strange because יום כפור is on the tenth. חייא will use this oddity to show that ערב יום כפור has its own special purpose. That purpose leaves no room for a long catch-up session.

keyTerms.meaning: חייא בר רב, from the town of דפתי
He taught him (quoted a teaching to him)
And you shall afflict your souls (the source for fasting)
On the ninth of the month

phrases.aramaic: תְּנָא לֵיהּ חִיָּיא בַּר רַב מִדִּפְתִּי:
phrases.english: Chiyya bar Rav of Difti taught him:
It is written: "And you shall afflict your souls
on the ninth of the month in the evening."

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא לֵיהּ חִיָּיא בַּר רַב מִדִּפְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ביבי's plan
steps.kashyaTarget: The plan to use ערב יום כפור to catch up on פרשיות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse shows that ערב יום כפור is set aside for something else (eating), so it should not be filled with reading.

steps.title: But the fast is on the tenth, not the ninth
steps.stepSummary: The verse seems to say we fast on the ninth, yet the fast is actually on the tenth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we fast on the ninth?! Don't we fast on the tenth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out the puzzle in the verse. It sets up the answer that explains what the verse really teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the same section, the תורה says the fast is "בעשור לחדש", on the tenth. So "בתשעה" cannot mean the actual fast day, and it must be teaching something extra.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it really so? (a surprised question)
But is it not so that

phrases.english: And do we fast on the ninth?!
But we fast on the tenth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the verse just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the verse mention the ninth, when the fast is on the tenth?

steps.title: Eating on the ninth counts like fasting on both days
steps.stepSummary: The verse teaches that one who eats and drinks on the ninth is credited as if he fasted on the ninth and the tenth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes to tell you: whoever eats and drinks on the ninth, the verse credits him as if he fasted on the ninth and the tenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the puzzle. The verse mentions the ninth to teach that eating on ערב יום כפור is itself a מצוה, worth as much as a fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since eating on ערב יום כפור has this special value, the day is meant for eating and drinking. It is not meant for a long session of catching up on פרשיות. So the verse answers רב ביבי's plan.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it comes to tell you
The verse credits him / considers it for him

steps.whatToRemember: Eating on ערב יום כפור is a מצוה. It counts as if one fasted two days, so that day is not the time to catch up on missed פרשיות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for the מצוה of eating on ערב יום כפור.

phrases.english: Rather, to tell you
anyone who eats and drinks on the ninth,
the verse credits him
as if he fasted on the ninth and the tenth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the ninth
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse teaches that eating on the ninth is credited like fasting, so ערב יום כפור is for eating.

steps.title: רב ביבי then plans to read the פרשיות early
steps.stepSummary: After that objection, רב ביבי considered reading the פרשיות ahead of the ציבור instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: He thought to read them early.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי switches to a new plan: read the פרשיות ahead of schedule so he won't fall behind. This sets up one more objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His first idea was making them up late. Now he tries the opposite, reading them in advance, which would avoid the problem of a backlog.

keyTerms.meaning: To do them early / in advance

phrases.english: He thought to read them early,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new plan after the first one was rejected
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposed practice: read the פרשיות before the ציבור does.

steps.title: An elder rules: not early and not late
steps.stepSummary: An elder quoted a teaching that one may not read the פרשיות before or after the ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain elder said to him: We learned, "Provided that one does not read early and does not read late."
steps.whatsHappening: An unnamed elder rejects the plan to read early. He quotes a teaching that the reading must match the ציבור's timing exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains the words "עם הצבור" (with the congregation). The point is not only to finish the פרשה, but to finish it in step with the ציבור. Reading early and reading late are both ruled out.

keyTerms.meaning: That he not read early and not read late

steps.whatToRemember: The פרשה must be completed together with the ציבור. That means the same week they read it: not ahead of time, and not making it up afterward.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying a missed פרשה is worthless. The point is that the ideal מצוה of reading "עם הצבור" means keeping pace with the ציבור.

phrases.english: A certain elder said to him: We learned:
Provided that he not read early and not read late.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the plan to read early
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ביבי's plan to read the פרשיות in advance
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids reading early or late; it must be with the ציבור.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרשיות must be completed in step with the ציבור, neither early nor late.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: finish your פרשה together with the ציבור
steps.stepSummary: The elder's teaching is supported by רבי יהושע בן לוי, who told his sons to complete their פרשיות with the ציבור: מקרא twice and תרגום once.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יהושע בן לוי said to his sons: complete your weekly portions together with the congregation, reading the verses twice and the translation once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the elder's teaching that you should not read the פרשה before or after the ציבור. רבי יהושע בן לוי told his sons to finish it 'with the ציבור'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 6, רב ביבי wanted to read the פרשיות early, ahead of the ציבור. רבי יהושע בן לוי's words 'עם הציבור' show that the reading should match the ציבור's schedule, which is the elder's point. This also teaches the method of שנים מקרא ואחד תרגום.

keyTerms.meaning: Together with the congregation, in the same week
Reading the verse twice and the Aramaic translation once

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for the practice of שנים מקרא ואחד תרגום, and for doing it in the same week the ציבור reads that פרשה.
steps.confusionAlert: 'With the ציבור' does not mean sitting in shul while the Torah is read aloud. It means finishing your own private reading in step with the ציבור's weekly schedule.

phrases.aramaic: כְּדַאֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי לִבְנֵיהּ:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said to his sons:
phrases.notes: The word 'as' links this back to the elder's teaching.

phrases.english: Complete your portions with the congregation
the verse twice and the translation once.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדַאֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי לִבְנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the elder's teaching in Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one should not read the פרשיות before or after the ציבור
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן לוי's instruction to his sons: 'אשלימו פרשיותייכו עם הציבור'

steps.title: Be careful to cut the jugular veins, like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי also told his sons to be careful about the ורידין in שחיטה, following רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And be careful with the jugular veins, following רבי יהודה. As we learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה says: the bird is not fit until he slaughters the jugular veins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to more of רבי יהושע בן לוי's advice to his sons. He told them to be careful to cut the ורידין when slaughtering, as רבי יהודה says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main rule of שחיטה is about the windpipe and food pipe. רבי יהודה adds the ורידין for a bird, so that blood will not stay inside it. רבי יהושע בן לוי advises following רבי יהודה as an extra level of care, even though this is not the basic requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: The jugular veins (blood vessels in the neck)
As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: And be careful with the jugular veins, like Rabbi Yehuda,
as we learned in a mishna: Rabbi Yehuda says:
[it is not valid] until he slaughters the jugular veins.
phrases.notes: This refers to slaughtering a bird. Cutting the veins keeps blood from staying in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of רבי יהושע בן לוי's instructions to his sons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Be careful in שחיטה to cut the ורידין, following רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Respect an elder who forgot his learning, like the broken tablets
steps.stepSummary: Keep honoring a זקן who forgot his Torah because of hardship he could not control, just as the broken לוחות were kept in the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And be careful about an elder who forgot his learning because of circumstances beyond his control. As we say: the tablets and the broken pieces of the tablets were placed in the Ark.
steps.whatsHappening: This is רבי יהושע בן לוי's third piece of advice: keep respecting a Torah scholar who forgot what he learned because of illness or hardship. He proves it from the broken לוחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that once an elder no longer remembers his Torah, he no longer deserves special honor. The proof says otherwise: משה broke the first לוחות, yet they still sat in the ארון beside the new ones. Holiness that was once there still deserves respect.

keyTerms.meaning: The broken pieces of the first tablets

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic source for honoring older scholars who have lost their memory or ability. Their honor stays with them.

phrases.english: And be careful with an elder who forgot his learning
because of circumstances beyond his control.
As we say:
The tablets and the broken tablets
are placed in the Ark.
phrases.notes: The broken first tablets were kept, not thrown away. The elder is compared to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next instruction in רבי יהושע בן לוי's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An elder who forgot his Torah through hardship must still be treated with respect.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע בן לוי's three instructions to his sons: (1) finish the פרשה with the ציבור, שנים מקרא ואחד תרגום; (2) be careful with the ורידין like רבי יהודה; (3) respect a זקן who forgot his learning, like the שברי לוחות in the ארון.

steps.title: רבא's advice: do not cut meat on your hand
steps.stepSummary: רבא told his sons not to cut meat while holding it on their hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to his sons: when you cut meat, do not cut it on top of your hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings a new set of father-to-son advice, this time from רבא. His first instruction is not to cut meat while holding it on your hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the pattern of the previous steps: a great Sage gives practical guidance to his children. רבא only gives the rule here. The reason comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: On the back or palm of the hand

phrases.english: Rava said to his sons:
When you cut meat,
do not cut on your hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Switches from רבי יהושע בן לוי's advice to a similar list from רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not cut meat while holding it on your hand.

steps.title: Two reasons for רבא's advice: danger or a ruined meal
steps.stepSummary: Some say the reason is the danger of cutting yourself. Others say it is that a cut could spoil the meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: because of danger. And some say: because of ruining the meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא gave this advice and offers two different reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason is safety: you might cut your hand. The second reason is about the food: even a small cut can drip blood onto the meat and make it disgusting to eat. The practical advice is the same either way. Only the reason behind it differs.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (introduces a version or opinion)

phrases.english: Some say: because of danger.
And some say: because of ruining the meal.
phrases.notes: A little blood from a cut could spoil the meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבא's first instruction.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבא told his sons not to cut meat on their hand
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two views: either because of the danger of cutting oneself, or because a cut could ruin the meal.

steps.title: Two more pieces of advice from רבא
steps.stepSummary: רבא also told his sons not to sit on the bed of an ארמית, and not to pass behind a בית הכנסת while the ציבור is davening.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do not sit on the bed of an Aramean woman, and do not pass behind the synagogue at a time when the congregation is praying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps listing what רבא told his sons, adding two new pieces of advice. The next steps will explain each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the list from step 11, where רבא warned about cutting meat on your hand. Both new rules are short and unclear, so the גמרא will explain them one at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: The bed of an Aramean (non-Jewish) woman

phrases.english: And do not sit on the bed of an Aramean woman,
and do not pass behind the synagogue
at a time when the congregation is praying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of רבא's advice that began in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not sit on the bed of an ארמית, and do not pass behind a בית הכנסת while the ציבור is davening.

steps.title: Three ways to explain the bed of an Aramean woman
steps.stepSummary: Some say it means do not go to sleep without קריאת שמע. Others say it means do not marry a גיורת. Others say it literally means the bed of an ארמית.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Do not sit on the bed of an ארמית': some say this means do not sleep without reciting קריאת שמע. Others say it means do not marry a גיורת. And others say it means an actual ארמית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first piece of advice again so it can explain what it means. It gives three different explanations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two explanations treat the advice as a picture. Sleeping without קריאת שמע is acting like a non-Jew, and a גיורת comes from a non-Jewish background. The third explanation takes the words at face value.
steps.confusionAlert: Repeating the phrase 'do not sit on the bed of an ארמית' is not a new rule. The גמרא quotes it again only so it can explain it.

phrases.english: 'And do not sit on the bed of an Aramean woman':
phrases.notes: Re-quote of רבא's words in order to explain them.

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי לָא תִּגְנוֹ בְּלָא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע,
phrases.english: some say: do not go to sleep without the Shema,
and some say: that you should not marry a convert.
And some say: an actual Aramean woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first piece of advice from step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'the bed of an ארמית' mean?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three views: sleeping without קריאת שמע, marrying a גיורת, or literally an ארמית's bed.

steps.title: The story of רב פפא and the hidden dead baby
steps.stepSummary: The literal reading comes from a story. רב פפא refused to sit on an ארמית's bed until she lifted it, and a dead baby was found underneath. From this the חכמים forbade sitting on such a bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is because of an incident with רב פפא. He went to an ארמית, and she brought out a bed and told him to sit. He said he would not sit until she lifted the bed. She lifted it, and they found a dead baby there. From this the חכמים said: it is forbidden to sit on the bed of an ארמית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that explains where the literal rule came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב פפא had sat down, he could have been blamed for killing the baby. The story shows a real danger of being framed, which supports reading the rule literally.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא (a sage of the גמרא)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that some rules of the חכמים are protective. They keep a person from being falsely blamed.

phrases.english: And this is because of the incident of Rav Pappa.
For Rav Pappa went to an Aramean woman,
she brought out a bed for him.
She said to him: Sit!
He said to her: I will not sit
until you lift up the bed.
She lifted up the bed
and they found a dead baby there.
From here the Sages said:
It is forbidden to sit on the bed of an Aramean woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the third, literal explanation in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The literal reading: actually not sitting on an ארמית's bed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב פפא and the dead baby found under the bed.

steps.title: The rule about passing behind a shul matches רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: רבא's advice not to pass behind a בית הכנסת during davening supports רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And do not pass behind the בית הכנסת while the ציבור is praying': this supports רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said that it is forbidden for a person to pass behind a בית הכנסת while the ציבור is praying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבא's second piece of advice. It points out that רבי יהושע בן לוי taught the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Passing behind the shul during davening looks like the person does not want to join the ציבור, which shows disrespect. רבא's advice and רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling back each other up.

keyTerms.meaning: It is forbidden for a person

phrases.english: 'And do not pass behind the synagogue
phrases.notes: Re-quote of רבא's second piece of advice.

phrases.english: when the congregation is praying':

phrases.aramaic: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי.
phrases.english: this supports Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.
For Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: אָסוּר לוֹ לְאָדָם שֶׁיַּעֲבוֹר אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת
phrases.english: It is forbidden for a person to pass behind a synagogue
when the congregation is praying.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second piece of advice from step 13 by linking it to רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's ban on passing behind a בית הכנסת during davening.

steps.title: First limit: only when there is no other entrance
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the ban applies only if the shul has no other entrance. If there is another door, it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We only said this when there is no other entrance. But if there is another entrance, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts to narrow רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule. This is the first of three limits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is another door, people will assume he is walking around to use it, so no one will suspect him. The rule is only about how things look, so when there is no bad impression, there is no ban.

keyTerms.meaning: We have no problem with it (it is allowed)

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלֵיכָּא פִּתְחָא אַחֲרִינָא,
phrases.english: We only said this where there is no other entrance,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִיכָּא פִּתְחָא אַחֲרִינָא — לֵית לָן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: but if there is another entrance, we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלֵיכָּא פִּתְחָא אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of רבי יהושע בן לוי from step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban applies only when the shul has no other entrance.

steps.title: Second limit: only when there is no other shul
steps.stepSummary: The ban applies only if there is no other בית הכנסת in town. If there is another one, it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we only said this when there is no other synagogue. But if there is another synagogue, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his second limit on the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is another shul, people will think he is on his way to daven there. So there is no suspicion and no ban.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלֵיכָּא בֵּי כְנִישְׁתָּא אַחֲרִינָא,
phrases.english: And we only said this where there is no other synagogue,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִיכָּא בֵּי כְנִישְׁתָּא אַחֲרִינָא — לֵית לָן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: but if there is another synagogue, we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלֵיכָּא בֵּי כְנִישְׁתָּא אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second limit, built on the same pattern as step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban applies only when there is no other shul.

steps.title: Third limit: carrying a load, running, or wearing תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The ban applies only if the person is not carrying a load, not running, and not wearing תפילין. If any one of these is true, it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we only said this when he is not carrying a load, not running, and not wearing תפילין. But if one of these is true, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his last limit, which ends the discussion of this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone carrying a load or running is clearly busy with something urgent. Someone wearing תפילין is clearly a God-fearing person. In each case no one will think he is avoiding davening.
steps.whatToRemember: Passing behind a בית הכנסת during davening is forbidden because of how it looks. אביי allows it whenever there is a clear reason people will not suspect him: there is another door, there is another shul, or he is carrying a load, running, or wearing תפילין.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא דָּרֵי טוּנָא,
phrases.english: And we only said this where he is not carrying a load,
and not running, and not wearing tefillin,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִיכָּא חַד מֵהָנָךְ — לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: but if one of these is true, we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא דָּרֵי טוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third and last limit in אביי's series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban does not apply if he is carrying a load, running, or wearing תפילין.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא praises three habits of the מדיים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי עקיבא praising three good habits of the מדיים: they cut meat only on a table, kiss only the back of the hand, and hold private talks only in a field.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי עקיבא said, 'There are three things I like about the Medes. When they cut meat, they cut it only on a table. When they kiss, they kiss only the back of the hand. When they talk privately, they do it only in a field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists good manners worth copying, which fits the practical advice it has been giving, such as רבא's advice not to cut meat on your hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each habit protects something. Cutting on a table keeps you from cutting your hand. Kissing the hand avoids an unpleasant face-kiss. Talking in an open field keeps anyone from secretly overhearing.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא (a teaching of the תנאים outside the משנה)
The Medes, a nation allied with Persia
They hold counsel, meaning they discuss private plans

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Akiva said:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים אוֹהֵב אֲנִי אֶת הַמָּדִיִּים,
phrases.english: For three things I like the Medes:
When they cut meat,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חוֹתְכִין אֶלָּא עַל גַּבֵּי הַשּׁוּלְחָן,
phrases.english: they cut only on top of the table;
phrases.notes: Not on the hand, which matches רבא's earlier advice

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁנּוֹשְׁקִין — אֵין נוֹשְׁקִין אֶלָּא עַל גַּב הַיָּד,
phrases.english: when they kiss, they kiss only on the back of the hand;
and when they take counsel, they take counsel only in the field.
phrases.notes: In an open field, nobody can hide nearby and listen

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים אוֹהֵב אֲנִי אֶת הַמָּדִיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of practical life advice with a parallel teaching of good manners.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Copy the Medes: cut meat on a table, kiss the back of the hand, and hold private talks in a field.

steps.title: Source verse for holding private talks in a field
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה shows that taking counsel in a field comes from יעקב, who called רחל and לאה out to the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: What is the verse that teaches this? 'And יעקב sent and called רחל and לאה to the field, to his flock.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to support the third habit, holding private talks in a field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעקב was planning to run away from לבן, and he needed privacy. He did not talk to his wives at home. He called them out to the field, so the habit of the מדיים is really an old Torah lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse? Asks for the פסוק that serves as a source

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
What is the verse that shows this?
"And Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah
to the field, to his flock" (Genesis 31:4).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as the source for the last habit in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: The practice of holding private talks only in a field
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית לא:ד, where יעקב calls רחל and לאה to the field

steps.title: רבן גמליאל praises the modesty of the פרסיים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבן גמליאל praising the פרסיים for being modest in three areas: eating, the bathroom, and marital relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבן גמליאל said, 'There are three things I like about the Persians. They are modest when they eat, modest in the bathroom, and modest in another matter.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, parallel ברייתא praising another nation, this time for צניעות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list has the same form as רבי עקיבא's list: 'three things I like.' The theme here is צניעות. 'Another matter' is a polite way of referring to marital relations.

keyTerms.meaning: Another matter, a polite term for marital relations

steps.confusionAlert: 'דבר אחר' here does not mean 'another explanation,' as it often does in the גמרא. Here it is a polite way to say marital relations.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabban Gamliel said:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים אוֹהֵב אֲנִי אֶת הַפַּרְסִיִּים:
phrases.english: For three things I like the Persians:
They are modest in their eating,
and modest in the bathroom,
and modest in another matter.
phrases.notes: A polite way of referring to marital relations

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים אוֹהֵב אֲנִי אֶת הַפַּרְסִיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ברייתא with the same 'three things I like' form, now about the פרסיים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פרסיים are praised for modesty in eating, in the bathroom, and in marital relations.

steps.title: The פרסיים are designated for גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains the פסוק 'I have commanded My consecrated ones' as referring to the פרסיים, who are 'set aside' for גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'I have commanded My consecrated ones.' רב יוסף taught: These are the פרסיים, who are set aside and prepared for גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: After praising the פרסיים, the גמרא gives the other side of the picture: a teaching that they are destined for גיהנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ישעיה, הקב"ה sends the פרסיים to destroy בבל. רב יוסף reads 'מקודשי' not as 'holy' but as 'set aside.' They are tools of God's anger, and in the end they are set aside for punishment. So good manners in some areas do not make a nation righteous overall.

keyTerms.meaning: My consecrated ones; here read as 'set aside' for a purpose
גיהנם, the place of punishment after death

steps.confusionAlert: 'מקודשין' here does not mean holy. It means 'set aside' or 'designated,' the way קידושין sets a woman aside for her husband.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא can praise specific good habits of a nation, such as the manners of the מדיים and the modesty of the פרסיים, and still judge that nation harshly as a whole.

phrases.english: "I have commanded My consecrated ones" (Isaiah 13:3):
Rav Yosef taught:
These are the Persians,
who are set aside and designated for Gehenna.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנִי צִוֵּיתִי לִמְקֻדָּשָׁי, תָּנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a contrasting view right after the praise of the פרסיים in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'consecrated ones' of ישעיה are the פרסיים, who are set aside for גיהנם.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, and רב יהודה quotes שמואל that the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל, who says the night שמע may be read until dawn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says, etc. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא comes back to the משנה after a long side discussion. It gives a practical ruling that we follow רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the חכמים set midnight as the deadline for the night שמע, and רבן גמליאל said it lasts until עמוד השחר (dawn). שמואל rules like רבן גמליאל, so the night שמע truly lasts all night. This ruling sets up the next ברייתא, which builds on רבן גמליאל's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא in the משנה who says the night שמע may be read until dawn
The practical law follows the opinion of...
'Etc.': the rest of the quote is not written out

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבן גמליאל: the night קריאת שמע may be read all night, until עמוד השחר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical ruling about the latest time for the evening שמע, and the rest of this passage builds on it.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says, etc.:
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, showing that the גמרא is returning to it

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabban Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about the מדיים and פרסיים and returns to the משנה's dispute about the night שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבן גמליאל: the night שמע may be read until dawn.

steps.title: Reading שמע twice around dawn
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון בן יוחי: sometimes a person reads שמע twice 'at night,' once before dawn and once after, and fulfills both his night and his day obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: sometimes a person reads שמע twice at night, once before dawn and once after dawn. With these he fulfills his obligation: one counts for the day and one for the night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that applies רבן גמליאל's view. A person can read שמע just before dawn for the night and just after dawn for the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the night שמע lasts until dawn, the reading right before dawn still counts for night. The ברייתא adds that the reading right after dawn already counts for the morning obligation. This sets up the next step, because the wording calls both readings 'at night.'

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who teaches this ברייתא
Dawn: the first light in the eastern sky

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says
there are times when a person reads Shema
twice at night,
once before dawn rises
and once after dawn rises,
and with them he fulfills his obligation

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל יוֹם וְאַחַת שֶׁל לַיְלָה.
phrases.english: one of the day and one of the night.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that works within רבן גמליאל's view that the night שמע lasts until dawn.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading שמע just before dawn counts for night, and reading it just after dawn counts for day.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא first calls the time after dawn 'night' and then says it counts as 'day.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא itself is difficult. You said: sometimes a person reads שמע twice at night. That shows the time after dawn is night. Then you taught: he fulfills his obligation, one of the day and one of the night. That shows it is day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא contradicts itself. The beginning calls the time after dawn night, but the ending treats it as day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'twice at night' mean both readings, including the one after dawn, happen at night. But 'one of the day' means the reading after dawn counts as the daytime שמע. So which is it: day or night?

keyTerms.meaning: 'This itself is difficult': the source contradicts itself
'And then it teaches': points to a later part of the same source

phrases.english: This itself is difficult,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרַתְּ: פְּעָמִים שֶׁאָדָם קוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע
phrases.english: you said: there are times when a person reads Shema
twice at night,

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא לְאַחַר שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר לֵילְיָא הוּא,
phrases.english: which shows that after dawn rises, it is night,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי: יוֹצֵא בָּהֶן יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ
phrases.english: and then it teaches: with them he fulfills his obligation

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל יוֹם וְאַחַת שֶׁל לַיְלָה,
phrases.english: one of the day and one of the night,
which shows that it is day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Its opening calls the time after dawn night, but its ending treats that same time as day. That is an internal contradiction.

steps.title: It is really night, but some people already get up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the time right after dawn really is night. The ברייתא calls it 'day' because some people get up at that hour.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It really is night. The reason it is called 'day' is that there are people who get up at that hour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. The time after dawn is truly night, but it can count as 'when you rise' because some people are already up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beginning of the ברייתא ('at night') is taken literally. The word 'day' in the ending does not mean real daytime. It means the morning-שמע מצוה of 'ובקומך' (when you rise) can be fulfilled then, since some people rise at that time.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Actually' or 'in truth': introduces the real answer

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying dawn is daytime. It says the opposite: it is still night. It counts for the morning שמע only because the מצוה is tied to 'when you rise,' and some people rise then.
steps.whatToRemember: The time just after עמוד השחר is still night. You can still fulfill the morning שמע then, because it counts as 'when you rise.'

phrases.english: No, it really is night.
And the reason it calls it 'day':
because there are people who get up
at that hour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of one word: 'day' means 'time of rising,' not literal daytime
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to treat the time after dawn as both night and day.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is really night. It is called 'day' only because some people rise then, so it counts for the morning שמע of 'when you rise.'

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן יוחי
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר חנינא, quoting רבי יהושע בן לוי, rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן יוחי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר חנינא said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן יוחי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a practical ruling on the ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחי that we just learned. That ברייתא said you can read שמע before dawn for night and after dawn for day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this first version, the ruling backs up רבי שמעון בן יוחי's earlier statement. That statement said a reading just before עמוד השחר counts for the night שמע, and a second reading just after עמוד השחר counts for the day שמע. Now that idea is not just one opinion; it is the accepted הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows (the opinion of...)
An early אמורא of ארץ ישראל, quoted here by רב אחא בר חנינא

steps.whyThisMatters: Pay attention to this ruling, because the very next line will argue about which statement of רבי שמעון בן יוחי it actually refers to.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Chanina said
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai.
phrases.notes: In this version, it refers to the ברייתא from step 25 (reading שמע twice, around dawn).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחי that was just explained in steps 25-27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן יוחי's ברייתא about reading שמע twice, once before dawn and once after.

steps.title: Another version: the ruling refers to a different ברייתא about sunrise
steps.stepSummary: Some say רב אחא בר חנינא's ruling was really said about a different ברייתא. In it, רבי שמעון בן יוחי quotes רבי עקיבא: a person may read שמע twice 'in the day', once before sunrise and once after, and so fulfill both his night and his day obligations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some people teach רב אחא בר חנינא's ruling as referring to this: As a ברייתא teaches, רבי שמעון בן יוחי says in the name of רבי עקיבא: Sometimes a person reads קריאת שמע twice in the day, once before sunrise and once after sunrise, and with them he fulfills his obligation, one of the day and one of the night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of where רב אחא בר חנינא's ruling belongs. It then quotes the ברייתא that this version attaches the ruling to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling itself does not change. Only its 'address' changes: it now refers to a ברייתא that רבי שמעון בן יוחי says in the name of רבי עקיבא. This ברייתא talks about sunrise (הנץ החמה), not dawn, and it calls both readings 'in the day.'

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach (a different version)
On this (referring to a different source)

steps.confusionAlert: This is a DIFFERENT ברייתא from the one in step 25. That one spoke about dawn (עמוד השחר) and called both readings 'at night.' This one speaks about sunrise (הנץ החמה), quotes רבי עקיבא, and calls both readings 'in the day.'

steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן יוחי in the name of רבי עקיבא: reading שמע once before sunrise and once after counts for both night and day.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself about the time before sunrise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that this ברייתא calls the reading before sunrise 'in the day.' Yet it also says that reading counts for the night obligation, so is that time day or night?
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא itself is difficult! You said 'sometimes a person reads קריאת שמע twice in the day,' so apparently the time before sunrise is day. And then it teaches 'he fulfills his obligation, one of the day and one of the night,' so apparently it is night!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא from the inside: its opening and its ending seem to disagree. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening words 'twice in the day' mean the reading before sunrise happens in daytime. But the ending says that same reading fulfills the night obligation, which only makes sense if it is still night. The ברייתא can't seem to have it both ways.

keyTerms.meaning: This itself is difficult (it contradicts itself)
And then it goes on to teach

so apparently it is night!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in step 29 by showing an internal contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחי in the name of רבי עקיבא (step 29)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The opening says both readings are 'in the day,' so the time before sunrise is day. The ending says one reading counts for the night obligation, so the time before sunrise is night. These two cannot both be true.
